# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The user approved, and commits were pushed after that.** In Sprint 3 a PR may only be merged
  after an approval on its latest commit, so it needs a new approval. Check only the new commits,
  as in a follow-up, and suggest a short re-approval if they're fine.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is a mutation-testing write-up** (`docs/sprint3/mutation/**`). If it holds only the
  write-up and the reports, treat it like a docs PR. If it also adds or changes a test, run that test
  (section 4) and check it the way section 5 describes. Also check that the mutant the write-up says
  it kills shows as killed in the `-after` report. Search the report for that location rather than
  reading it whole, since the reports can be large.
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, including its `## Test Evidence` section, and the linked issue's
   acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions. The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. The review bots' comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed:
   - **CodeRabbit**, configured by the repo's `.coderabbit.yaml`.
   - **Gitar** (Sonar's AI reviewer, mentioned as `@gitar-bot`), if the team turns it on. It keeps
     one dashboard comment that it updates on every push, holding its verdict and, when CI fails, a
     root-cause analysis. It also posts inline findings rated Critical, Important or Minor, and moves
     resolved ones into a collapsed section. Its rules, if any, are in the repo's `.gitar/` folder.
4. The CI status, if you can see it. Gitar's root-cause note on a failure is a lead, not a verdict;
   check it. If the course connects the repo to SonarQube Cloud, its quality gate shows up among the
   PR's checks.
5. SonarQube for IDE, if it's running in the user's VS Code and Claude Code is connected (`/ide`).
   Read its diagnostics for the PR's changed files. Only findings on changed lines count, and each is
   a lead to check like any other finding. If nothing shows, skip this step rather than setting it up.
6. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint; CI does that. Do run the PR's tests (section 4), so the user doesn't have to. Don't
split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls for reading and checking, plus what the test runs need. In testing,
runs that went to 35 calls produced no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls
on checking the findings that will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't
include. Don't read the author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends
on it. If you go over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.
Reviewers are expected to answer within 24 hours, which is one more reason to keep it short.

## 4. Run the PR's tests

In the clone, run the tests the PR adds or changes, plus the existing test files for the source files
it changes, and record the real counts. In chat you can't run anything: say so, give the user the exact
commands to run, and leave the testing line as a TODO.

- **Work in a throwaway worktree**, so the user's branch and their own server aren't touched:
  `git worktree add --detach .specstory/review-<N> pr-<N>`, then `CI=true pnpm install
  --frozen-lockfile` inside it. Never symlink `node_modules` into a worktree.
- **Unit tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run <files>` for the frontend, and `go test -run '<names>' ./<pkg>/`
  for Go. Go must match `go.mod`: a newer system Go breaks things, so put `~/sdk/go1.26.4/bin` first on
  `PATH` (check `go version` against `go.mod`).
- **Can the new unit tests fail?** This check is cheap. Restore the PR's changed source files to
  `origin/main` in the worktree, re-run the new unit tests, then restore the PR's versions. Tests for
  new behaviour should now fail. One that still passes may not test the change. Use it as evidence for
  the Test coverage row, not as a finding on its own.
- **Playwright tests the PR adds or changes:** `make test-e2e` can't run on this machine.
  1. Build the worktree (`make frontend backend`).
  2. Start its own server from a copy of `custom/conf/app.ini` with `WORK_PATH` set to the worktree
     and port 3001. Start it inside a helper script and stop it by PID, never with `pkill -f`. Create
     the `e2e-admin` user (password `password`) with `./gitea admin user create` if that instance
     doesn't have it.
  3. Run Playwright with a scratch config that extends `playwright.config.ts` and points Chromium at
     `/usr/bin/chromium` (`launchOptions.executablePath`). Set `GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL`,
     `GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER=e2e-admin`, `GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD=password` and
     `GITEA_TEST_E2E_DOMAIN=localhost`. Run on Chromium and Firefox.

  If the setup still fails after one fix, stop and say so; CI's e2e run is the fallback. The shell is
  zsh, so write environment variables out instead of using unquoted `$VARS`.
- **Read only the summary lines** of each run (pass, fail and skip counts, plus the names of any
  failures), not the full output.
- **A failure isn't a finding yet.** `multiselect-aria.test.ts` already fails locally on untouched
  main, and CI passes it. For any other failure, re-run it on `origin/main`. Only a failure the PR
  causes is a required fix, because the course allows no new test failures.
- **Clean up:** stop the server, then `git worktree remove --force .specstory/review-<N>`.

On a follow-up after new commits, re-run only the tests those commits touch.

## 5. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **The Test Evidence section** (required in every PR since Sprint 3). It needs:
  - one row per AC (for a bug fix, its Expected Behavior; for a PR with no behaviour change, "N/A"
    and a reason);
  - for each row, a named test or "Manual:" steps with what was seen;
  - a Level of unit, integration, E2E or manual;
  - a Source of expected value of AC, issue discussion, docs, upstream behavior, or other
    (explained);
  - a "Not tested automatically, and why" line that lists only the manual ACs;
  - an "AI-written tests" line, saying which tests and how their expected values were checked.

  Spot-check one or two rows: open the test, read its expected value, and compare it with the cited
  source. A value that only matches what the code happens to output (a pasted snapshot, or a number
  the AC never mentions) is exactly what the sprint page rules out.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - `Closes #<N>` in the description, and the PR on the `Sprint 3` milestone;
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer;
  - a skipped test, `test.fail()`, `t.Skip` or disabled CI check has a linked issue and a reason in
    a code comment;
  - no new test failures: a red CI check on code the PR touches is a required fix;
  - commits pushed by a bot (for example a Gitar fix) are AI-made changes, so the AI section should
    mention them.

  A bot's approval (Gitar can auto-approve) doesn't count: the course needs a teammate's approval.

  The current sprint's rules are on https://csci-435-se.github.io/sprint3/. The repo's
  `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md` still described Sprint 2 on Nov 4, so where the two
  disagree, the sprint page wins.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit or Gitar findings the author already
fixed (credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score. A bot or Sonar finding
that's still open goes in the draft only if you checked it against the code yourself. A Sonar rule
that fights Gitea's conventions isn't a finding.

## 6. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

The test-evidence row is new, so there are no posted examples of it yet. Score it like the other
rows. A missing Test Evidence section, an AC with no row, or an expected value with no real source is
a required fix and lowers the score. A source that is valid but could be stronger is optional and
leaves it at 10. The row also asks which tests the reviewer ran locally: answer it from the section 4
runs, with real counts. If nothing could be run, put a visible `TODO (you): which tests you ran
locally` there instead.

## 7. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 3: the sprint page adds the test-evidence row. On Nov 4 the repo's rubric file didn't
have that row yet, so keep it even if the file still lacks it.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

Ran the PR's tests locally with Claude Code: <each command or file, with its pass/fail/skip counts>. TODO (you): anything you clicked or checked by hand, or delete this.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | <finding>. Ran <which tests> locally: <counts>. |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** states only the test runs that really happened in section 4, with their
  counts, and says Claude Code ran them. What the user clicked or checked by hand stays a visible
  `TODO` for them to write or delete. Never fill it with your own checks; a visible placeholder can't
  be posted by accident without being noticed.

## 8. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- the test results, and what you didn't run or check (for example, "e2e setup failed, so I relied
  on CI"), so the user knows what is left for them;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log in `ai-logs/sprint3/ab-wm/`, as
`ai-logs/README.md` describes, since the AI-Log section points to it. If they approve, mention once
that any commit the author pushes afterwards needs a new approval before the merge.

```text
S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151

## User Story
As a PR author, I want a reviewer's suggested code to show as a before/after diff in the review
comment so that I can see exactly what would change without comparing it to the file myself.

### User Scenario

## User Scenario
Ana reviews PR #42. On line 18 of `main.go` she writes a code comment containing

````markdown
```suggestion
	return fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", name, err)
```
````

and submits the review. Ben, the author, opens the Conversation tab. Under Ana's comment he sees
a small diff: line 18 as it is now in red, her replacement in green, labelled "Suggested change".
The same rendering appears on the Files changed tab. Text outside the block renders as normal
markdown.


### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a code comment on a new-side line whose body has one ```` ```suggestion ```` block,
  when the comment is shown in the Conversation or Files changed tab, then the block renders as a
  diff headed "Suggested change": the commented line as removed (red) and each line of the block
  as added (green), with indentation kept.
- [ ] AC2: Given an empty ```` ```suggestion ```` block, when rendered, then it shows the commented
  line as removed and nothing added (a "delete this line" suggestion).
- [ ] AC3: Given a ```` ```suggestion ```` block in a plain issue or PR comment (not a code
  comment), when rendered, then it shows as an ordinary code block, not a diff.
- [ ] AC4: Given a code comment with two or more suggestion blocks, when rendered, then each block
  renders as its own diff against the same commented line. (S3 decides whether to offer Apply.)
- [ ] AC5: Given suggestion content containing HTML such as `<script>alert(1)</script>`, when
  rendered, then it is shown as literal text and nothing is executed.
- [ ] AC6: Given an outdated code comment (the branch moved and the comment is `Invalidated`), when
  rendered, then the diff is still shown against the line the reviewer originally commented on,
  next to the existing "Outdated" label.
- [ ] AC7: Given a code comment on an old-side (deleted) line, or one whose stored diff context is
  missing, when rendered, then the suggestion block shows as an ordinary code block and the page
  has no errors.
- [ ] AC8: Given a code comment with a suggestion is edited, when the edit is saved, then the
  updated block renders as a diff without reloading the page.

### Out of Scope

- Applying the suggestion (S3); multi-line ranges (S5); the editor button (S2).
- Suggestions in commit comments outside a PR (#151 out of scope).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines, until the customer answers question 5 on #151.
- Syntax highlighting inside the suggestion diff.

### Open Questions

- Should the old side of the diff come from the comment's stored diff context (what the reviewer
  saw) or from the file at the current head? (Decided: stored context, so the diff never changes
  under the reader; S3 does the "has it changed since" check.)
- Old-side suggestions: waiting on customer question 5 on #151.


### Design Decision

**Decision:** Render the diff in the browser, the same way Gitea already renders `mermaid` and
`math` code blocks. The server takes the commented line from the comment's stored diff context
(`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always the commented line) through a new
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` method, and puts it in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute
on the body of new-side code comments only. A new `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`, registered
beside the mermaid and math handlers, replaces each `code.language-suggestion` block inside such a
body with a diff, building it with `textContent` only.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Post-process the rendered HTML on the server.* After markdown renders a code comment, Go would
  find the `<pre><code class="language-suggestion">` and swap in a template-rendered diff. It works
  without JavaScript, but it rewrites already-sanitised HTML and has to be repeated in both places
  that render code comments (the page load and the edit-comment save).
- *A markdown renderer extension in `modules/markup`.* The renderer would emit the diff directly,
  but it would need to know which file and line a comment belongs to, which it doesn't carry for
  any other content, and the sanitiser's allowlist would need new classes.

**Rationale:** It follows an existing pattern (mermaid, math), leaves the markdown renderer and
sanitiser untouched, and the attribute on new-side code comments only is what keeps plain comments
as plain code blocks (AC3). Editing a comment re-runs the same frontend hook, so AC8 needs no
extra server code.

**Consequences:** Without JavaScript a suggestion shows as a plain code block. S3 and S7 must find
suggestion blocks in Go themselves (using goldmark's parser, so they agree with what the page
shows); S1 gives them `SuggestionOriginalLine()` to compare against.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Medium scope because it touches a good amount of components in the code
```
</details></tool-use>

diff --git a/models/issues/comment_suggestion.go b/models/issues/comment_suggestion.go
new file mode 100644

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package issues
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+
+	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
+)
+
+// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
+// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
+// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
+func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
+	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
+		return optional.None[string]()
+	}
+	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
+	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
+	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
+		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
+	}
+	return optional.Some(last[1:])
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package issues_test
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine(t *testing.T) {
+	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n"
+	cases := []struct {
+		name     string
+		typ      issues_model.CommentType
+		line     int64
+		patch    string
+		expected optional.Option[string]
+	}{
+		{"added line keeps indentation", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 3, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil\n+\treturn err", optional.Some("\treturn err")},
+		{"context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n func main() {}", optional.Some("func main() {}")},
+		{"trailing newline in patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n+x := 1\n", optional.Some("x := 1")},
+		{"blank context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n ", optional.Some("")},
+		{"CRLF kept", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 1, header + "+foo\r", optional.Some("foo\r")},
+		{"old side is not supported", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, -2, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil", optional.None[string]()},
+		{"removed line on new side is inconsistent", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n-gone", optional.None[string]()},
+		{"empty patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, "", optional.None[string]()},
+		{"header only", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header, optional.None[string]()},
+		{"not a code comment", issues_model.CommentTypeComment, 2, header + "+x", optional.None[string]()},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			comment := &issues_model.Comment{Type: c.typ, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch}
+			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
+		})
+	}
+}

+func TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute(t *testing.T) {

+		}, true)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+
+		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
+			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
+			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
+				Operation:     "update",

+				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n\treturn err\n"),

+import {initMarkupCodeSuggestion} from './suggestion.ts';
+
+function makeMarkup(attrs: Record<string, string>, body: string): HTMLElement {
+  const el = document.createElement('div');
+  el.className = 'render-content markup';
+  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) el.setAttribute(k, v);
+  el.innerHTML = body;
+  return el;
+}
+
+function codeBlock(text: string, lang = 'suggestion'): string {
+  return `<div class="code-block-container code-overflow-scroll"><pre class="code-block"><code class="chroma language-${lang} display">${text}</code></pre></div>`;
+}
+
+const attrs = {'data-suggestion-original': '\treturn err', 'data-suggestion-label': 'Suggested change'};
+
+function rows(el: Element) {
+  return Array.from(el.querySelectorAll('.markup-suggestion-line'), (row) => ({
+    kind: row.classList.contains('removed') ? 'removed' : 'added',
+    text: row.querySelector('code')!.textContent,
+  }));
+}
+
+test('renders the original line as removed and each block line as added', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, `<p>try this</p>${codeBlock('\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)\n\treturn nil\n')}`);
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(el.querySelector('.code-block-container')).toBeNull();
+  const diff = el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')!;
+  expect(diff.querySelector('.markup-suggestion-header')!.textContent).toEqual('Suggested change');
+  expect(rows(diff)).toEqual([
+    {kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'},
+    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)'},
+    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn nil'},
+  ]);
+  expect(el.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toEqual('try this');
+});
+
+test('empty block only removes the line', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock(''));
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(rows(el)).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}]);
+});
+
+test('one blank line replaces the line with a blank line', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('\n')); // what the renderer emits for a fence holding one blank line
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(rows(el)).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}, {kind: 'added', text: ''}]);
+});
+
+test('capitalised Suggestion is an ordinary code block', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('x\n', 'Suggestion'));
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')).toBeNull();
+});
+
+test('each block gets its own diff against the same line', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('a\n') + codeBlock('b\n'));
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  const diffs = el.querySelectorAll('.markup-suggestion');
+  expect(diffs).toHaveLength(2);
+  expect(rows(diffs[1])).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}, {kind: 'added', text: 'b'}]);
+});
+
+test('HTML in a suggestion stays text', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('&lt;img src=x onerror=alert(1)&gt;\n'));
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(el.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();
+  expect(rows(el)[1].text).toEqual('<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>');
+});
+
+test('without the attribute nothing changes', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup({}, codeBlock('x\n'));
+  const before = el.innerHTML;
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(el.innerHTML).toEqual(before);
+});
+
+test('other languages are left alone', () => {
+  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('x\n', 'go'));
+  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
+  expect(el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')).toBeNull();
+});
diff --git a/web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts b/web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..29a834ce37
--- /dev/null
+++ b/web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+import {queryElems} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+
+function makeLine(kind: 'removed' | 'added', text: string): HTMLElement {
+  const row = document.createElement('div');
+  row.className = `markup-suggestion-line ${kind}`;
+  const marker = document.createElement('span');
+  marker.className = 'markup-suggestion-marker';
+  marker.textContent = kind === 'removed' ? '-' : '+';
+  const code = document.createElement('code');
+  code.textContent = text; // never innerHTML: suggestion text is user input
+  row.append(marker, code);
+  return row;
+}
+
+// Replaces ```suggestion blocks in a PR code comment with a diff against the commented line.
+// The server only sets data-suggestion-original on new-side code comments, so plain comments keep a code block.
+export function initMarkupCodeSuggestion(elMarkup: HTMLElement): void {
+  const original = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-original');
+  if (original === null) return;
+  const label = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-label')!;
+  queryElems(elMarkup, 'code.language-suggestion', (elCode) => {
+    const block = elCode.closest('.code-block-container') ?? elCode.closest('pre')!;
+    // an empty fence renders "" (delete the line); otherwise every line ends with "\n", so one blank line is "\n"
+    const raw = elCode.textContent;
+    const diff = document.createElement('div');
+    diff.className = 'markup-suggestion';
+    const header = document.createElement('div');
+    header.className = 'markup-suggestion-header';
+    header.textContent = label;
+    diff.append(header, makeLine('removed', original));
+    if (raw !== '') {
+      for (const line of raw.replace(/\r?\n$/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) diff.append(makeLine('added', line));
+    }
+    block.replaceWith(diff);
+  });
+}

import {initMarkupCodeMermaid} from './mermaid.ts';

import {initExternalRenderIframe} from './render-iframe.ts';
import {toggleElemClass} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// code that runs for all markup content
export function initMarkupContent(): void {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initExternalRenderIframe', initExternalRenderIframe);
  registerGlobalSelectorFunc('.markup', (el: HTMLElement) => {
    if (el.matches('.truncated-markup')) {
      // when the rendered markup is truncated (e.g.: user's home activity feed)
      // we should not initialize any of the features (e.g.: code copy button), due to:
      // * truncated markup already means that the container doesn't want to show complex contents
      // * truncated markup may contain incomplete HTML/mermaid elements
      // so the only thing we need to do is to remove the "is-loading" class added by the backend render.
      toggleElemClass(el.querySelectorAll('.is-loading'), 'is-loading', false);
      return;
    }
    initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el); // before code-copy, so replaced blocks never get a copy button
    initMarkupCodeCopy(el);
    initMarkupTasklist(el);
    initMarkupCodeMermaid(el);
    initMarkupCodeMath(el);
  });
}

  const saveAndRefresh = async (e: Event) => {
    e.preventDefault();

    // at the moment, the form submit event conflicts with initRepoDiffConversationForm (global '.conversation-holder form' event handler)
    e.stopPropagation();
    renderContent.classList.add('is-loading');

    try {
      const params = new URLSearchParams({
        content: comboMarkdownEditor.value(),
        context: String(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-context')),
        content_version: String(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-content-version')),
      });
      for (const file of comboMarkdownEditor.dropzoneGetFiles() ?? []) {
        params.append('files[]', file);
      }

      const response = await POST(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-update-url')!, {data: params});
      const data = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok) {
        showErrorToast(data?.errorMessage ?? window.config.i18n.error_occurred);
        return;
      }

      reinitializeAreYouSure(editContentZone.querySelector('form')); // the form is no longer dirty
      editContentZone.setAttribute('data-content-version', data.contentVersion);

      // replace the render content with new one, to trigger re-initialization of all features
      const newRenderContent = renderContent.cloneNode(false) as HTMLElement;
      newRenderContent.innerHTML = data.content;
      renderContent.replaceWith(newRenderContent);
      renderContent = newRenderContent;

BODY:
Closes #154

## What changed

A ```` ```suggestion ```` block in a PR code comment now renders as a small diff headed
"Suggested change": the commented line in red, the block's lines in green.

- **Model:** `Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` (`models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`) returns the
  commented line from the comment's stored diff context (`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always
  the commented line). It returns nothing for old-side comments, non-code comments and missing
  context.
- **Templates:** `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `repo/issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl` put that
  line in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute on the comment body, with the locale label
  `repo.diff.suggestion.title`. Only new-side code comments get it.
- **Frontend:** `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts` is registered in `markup/content.ts` next to the
  mermaid and math handlers. Inside bodies carrying the attribute, it replaces each
  `code.language-suggestion` block with the diff, built with `textContent` only. It runs before
  code-copy, so the diff gets no copy button.
- **CSS:** `web_src/css/markup/suggestion.css` uses the theme's diff row colours, so light and dark
  themes both work.

## Why

This is the first slice of #151: reviewers can propose an exact replacement for a line, and readers
see it as a change rather than as a bare code block. It satisfies AC1–AC9 of #154. Applying a
suggestion (S3), the editor button (S2) and multi-line ranges (S5) are separate issues.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: suggestion on a new-side code comment renders as a diff with "Suggested change", indentation kept, in both tabs and in replies | `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine` ("added line keeps indentation", "context line"); `TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute` subtests `diff`, `timeline`, "reply in the thread gets the attribute"; Vitest "renders the original line as removed and each block line as added"; Manual: commented on `\treturn err` in both tabs and saw a red `-` line and a green `+` line, tab kept | unit, integration, manual | AC (label text, red/green rows, indentation); the original line is the README content the test itself commits |
| AC2: an empty block deletes the line; one blank line replaces it with a blank line | Vitest "empty block only removes the line", "one blank line replaces the line with a blank line"; Manual: both cases on the Files tab (screenshot) | unit, manual | AC |
| AC3: suggestions in plain comments and review summaries stay code blocks | `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine` "not a code comment"; Vitest "without the attribute nothing changes"; Manual: a suggestion in the PR's main comment box and in a review summary both stayed code blocks | unit, manual | AC |
| AC4: two blocks give two diffs against the same line | Vitest "each block gets its own diff against the same line"; Manual: two blocks in one comment | unit, manual | AC |
| AC5: HTML in a suggestion is shown as text | Vitest "HTML in a suggestion stays text"; Manual: `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` and `<script>` showed as text, no element created, no alert | unit, manual | AC |

  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## What changed

Adds one integration test, `tests/integration/api_pull_review_suggestion_test.go`. A "lint bot" posts a review through the existing `POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews` with two code comments that hold a `suggestion` block, one on each side of the diff. The test then checks that:

- the API stores both comment bodies exactly as sent;
- on both the Files tab (`repo/diff/comments.tmpl`) and the Conversation tab (`view_content/conversation.tmpl`), only the new-side comment gets `data-suggestion-original`, set to the commented line, and the "Suggested change" label. That is the hook S1's client code uses to draw the diff;
- the old-side comment stays a plain `code.language-suggestion` block.

No production code changes.

## Why

AC1 of #160: *"Given a review created through the existing API with a suggestion block in a code comment, when viewed in the UI, then it renders as a suggestion … (no API change needed; integration test proves it)."* This is the evidence for the issue's design decision that bots don't need a new create endpoint. The "can be applied" half of AC1 depends on S3 and will be tested with the apply endpoint (AC2).

## Test Evidence

| AC | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 (stored as sent) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders`, the review-comments `GET` | Integration | The `suggestion` body the test posts |
| AC1 (renders as suggestion, Files tab) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders/files_tab` | Integration | `"\treturn err"` is line 2 of the README the test writes to the head branch; `"Suggested change"` is the `repo.diff.suggestion.title` locale string from #163; the replacement text is the posted block |
| AC1 (renders as suggestion, Conversation tab) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders/conversation_tab` | Integration | Same as above |
| AC1 (old side is not a suggestion) | Both subtests: exactly 1 of the 2 `language-suggestion` blocks is marked | Integration | #163 limits suggestions to new-side comments |

This is an integration test rather than a unit test because the AC is about the whole path: API handler → stored comment → page template.

**The test fails without the feature:** with S1's two templates reverted to their `main` versions, both subtests fail (`expected: 1, actual: 0`). With them restored, the test passes.

The client-side diff drawing is S1's code and is covered by its Vitest file (`web_src/js/markup/suggestion.test.ts`).

## CI / manual verification

- `make 'test-integration#TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders'` → `ok gitea.dev/tests/integration 5.1s`
- With S1's templates reverted to `main`: `files_tab` and `conversation_tab` both FAIL, as intended
- `golangci-lint run ./tests/integration/` → `0 issues`; `make fmt` → no changes

## Design

It follows #160's Design Decision ("No new create endpoint: suggestions stay markdown in the comment body"), and this test is the evidence that the decision works.

**Introduced:** The PR is stacked on #163, so it can't merge until S1 does. The test checks the server-side hook (`data-suggestion-original`), not the drawn diff, because drawing happens in the browser. ### User Story
As a bot or tool author, I want to create suggestions and apply them through `/api/v1` so that
automated reviewers (linters, formatters) can propose fixes that the author applies in Gitea.
### User Scenario
A lint bot posts a review via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews` with a comment
whose body has a suggestion block. Ben applies it in the UI. A release script calls
`POST .../pulls/comments/{id}/suggestion/apply` to apply another one.
### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a review created through the existing API with a suggestion block in a code
  comment, when viewed in the UI, then it renders as a suggestion and can be applied (no API
  change needed; integration test proves it).
- [ ] AC2: Given a token with `write:repository` and push access to the head branch, when it POSTs
  the apply endpoint, then the commit is created and the response contains the commit SHA.
- [ ] AC3: Given missing permission, an outdated suggestion, an already applied one, or a stale
  `head_sha`, when the endpoint is called, then it returns 403 / 409 / 409 / 409 with a message and
  commits nothing.
- [ ] AC4: Given `GET` on a review comment, when the suggestion was applied, then the response
  includes `suggestion_applied_by` and `suggestion_applied_commit`.
- [ ] AC5: Swagger is regenerated and the swagger check passes.
### Out of Scope
- A batch apply endpoint, unless S6 has landed (then add `comment_ids[]`).
### Open Questions
- Should the API also accept a structured `suggestion` field instead of only markdown in `body`?
### Design Decision
**Decision:** No new create endpoint: suggestions stay markdown in the comment body. Add one apply
endpoint that takes `head_sha` and an optional `message` and calls S3's service.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A structured create endpoint (`path`, `lines`, `replacement`).* Easier for bots, but two ways to
  author the same thing that must render identically.
- *Mirror GitHub's API shape exactly.* GitHub has no apply endpoint to mirror.
**Rationale:** Bots already post review comments through the existing API, so they get
suggestions for free, and the service layer is shared with the UI.
**Consequences:** New route and swagger entry (`docs/routers-api-v1.md`), new fields on the comment
API struct (`docs/modules-structs.md`).
### Scope
medium
### Scope Justification
Touches multiple components. Builds off S3
```

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// A bot posting a review through the existing API gets suggestions with no API change (#160 AC1).
func TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		const (
			commentedLine = "\treturn err" // line 2 of the head README, written below
			replacement   = "\treturn nil"
			suggestion    = "```suggestion\n" + replacement + "\n```"
		)

		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_api_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n" + commentedLine + "\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_api_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "API suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))

		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteRepository)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, http.MethodPost, fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/reviews", pr.Issue.Index), &api.CreatePullReviewOptions{
			Event: api.ReviewStateComment,
			Body:  "lint bot",
			Comments: []api.CreatePullReviewComment{
				{Path: "README.md", Body: suggestion, NewLineNum: 2},
				{Path: "README.md", Body: suggestion, OldLineNum: 1}, // old side: stays a plain code block
			},
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		review := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &api.PullReview{})
		assert.Equal(t, api.ReviewStateComment, review.State)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, review.CodeCommentsCount)

		req = NewRequestf(t, http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/repos/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/reviews/%d/comments", pr.Issue.Index, review.ID).AddTokenAuth(token)
		comments := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), []*api.PullReviewComment{})
		require.Len(t, comments, 2)
		for _, c := range comments {
			assert.Equal(t, suggestion, c.Body) // stored verbatim, no API-side rewriting
		}

		pages := map[string]string{ // repo/diff/comments.tmpl and view_content/conversation.tmpl
			"files tab":        fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/files", pr.Issue.Index),
			"conversation tab": fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d", pr.Issue.Index),
		}
		for name, link := range pages {
			t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
				doc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, link), http.StatusOK).Body)
				assert.Equal(t, 2, doc.Find(".render-content.markup code.language-suggestion").Length())

				markup := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]")
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length()) // only the new-side comment
				assert.Equal(t, commentedLine, markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Suggested change", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-label", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, replacement+"\n", markup.Find("code.language-suggestion").Text())
			})
		}
	})
}
```

Closes #154

## What changed

A ```` ```suggestion ```` block in a PR code comment now renders as a small diff headed
"Suggested change": the commented line in red, the block's lines in green.

- **Model:** `Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` (`models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`) returns the
  commented line from the comment's stored diff context (`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always
  the commented line). It returns nothing for old-side comments, non-code comments and missing
  context.
- **Templates:** `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `repo/issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl` put that
  line in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute on the comment body, with the locale label
  `repo.diff.suggestion.title`. Only new-side code comments get it.
- **Frontend:** `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts` is registered in `markup/content.ts` next to the
  mermaid and math handlers. Inside bodies carrying the attribute, it replaces each
  `code.language-suggestion` block with the diff, built with `textContent` only. It runs before
  code-copy, so the diff gets no copy button.
- **CSS:** `web_src/css/markup/suggestion.css` uses the theme's diff row colours, so light and dark
  themes both work.

## Why

This is the first slice of #151: reviewers can propose an exact replacement for a line, and readers
see it as a change rather than as a bare code block. It satisfies AC1–AC9 of #154. Applying a
suggestion (S3), the editor button (S2) and multi-line ranges (S5) are separate issues.

**Not tested automatically, and why:**
- **AC6** needs a push that invalidates a comment, which the existing integration helpers don't
  make cheap. It is also safe by construction: the diff reads the stored `Patch`, which an
  invalidation doesn't change.
- **AC8** is a browser-only flow (the edit swaps the body's HTML and the markup observer re-runs).
  There is no Playwright test for comment editing to extend yet.

- `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine` (10 cases)

I checked that each expected value comes from the AC text or from data the test sets up itself,
never from the code's output. The integration test was run and failed before the template change,
then passed after it.

## Design

As in the Design Decision on #154: render in the browser the same way mermaid and math are, with
the server providing the original line through a data attribute. Nothing changed from the
approved design.

## Tech Debt


**Introduced:**
- **Slow integration test:** `TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute` takes about 9s locally, against
  the under-2s target. Almost all of that is creating the repo, the branch and the PR. The subtests
  share one PR to keep it down.
- **No-JavaScript fallback:** without JavaScript, a suggestion shows as a plain code block (an
  accepted consequence of the design).
- **Old-side comments:** suggestions on deleted lines are deliberately left as code blocks until
  the customer answers question 5 on #151.

**Encountered:** None.

modules/git/diff.go
func CutDiffAroundLine(originalDiff io.Reader, line int64, old bool, numbersOfLine int) (string, error) {
	if line == 0 || numbersOfLine == 0 {
		// no line or num of lines => no diff
		return "", nil
	}

	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(originalDiff)
	hunk := make([]string, 0)

	// begin is the start of the hunk containing searched line
	// end is the end of the hunk ...
	// currentLine is the line number on the side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	// otherLine is the line number on the opposite side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	var begin, end, currentLine, otherLine int64
	var headerLines int

	inHunk := false

	for scanner.Scan() {
		lof := scanner.Text()
		// Add header to enable parsing

		if isHeader(lof, inHunk) {
			if strings.HasPrefix(lof, cmdDiffHead) {
				inHunk = false
			}
			hunk = append(hunk, lof)
			headerLines++
		}
		if currentLine > line {
			break
		}
		// Detect "hunk" with contains commented lof
		if strings.HasPrefix(lof, "@@") {
			inHunk = true
			// Already got our hunk. End of hunk detected!
			if len(hunk) > headerLines {
				break
			}
			// A map with named groups of our regex to recognize them later more easily
			submatches := hunkRegex.FindStringSubmatch(lof)
			groups := make(map[string]string)
			for i, name := range hunkRegex.SubexpNames() {
				if i != 0 && name != "" {
					groups[name] = submatches[i]
				}
